Question:
Viswam walks half a mile to get to school each day. His route consists of \(10\) city blocks of equal length and he takes one minute to walk each block. Today, after walking \(5\) blocks, Viswam discovers that he has to make a detour, walking \(3\) blocks of equal length instead of \(1\) block to reach the next corner. From the time he starts his detour, at what speed, in miles per hour, must Viswam walk in order to arrive at school at his usual time?

[Figure 1](figures/2023_AMC_8_Q15_question_fig1.svg)
Solution:
At the start of the detour, Viswam has already used \(5\) of his usual \(10\) minutes. He therefore has \(5\) minutes left. The detour replaces one remaining block with three, adding \(2\) blocks, so he must now walk \(5+2=7\) blocks in that time.

Ten blocks make \(\frac12\) mile, so one block is \(\frac1{20}\) mile. The remaining distance is \(\frac7{20}\) mile, and the remaining time is \(\frac5{60}=\frac1{12}\) hour. His required speed is

\[
\frac{\frac7{20}\text{ mile}}{\frac1{12}\text{ hour}}
=\frac{84}{20}=\boxed{4.2}\text{ miles per hour},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\). The speed is calculated from the distance and time still available when the detour begins.
